text: DSH Superpowers 是面向 Web 客户端的规格驱动开发 Agent 预设。它将 Superpowers 技能目录、引导 persona 和委派工具组合进 DSH，并提供按技能和默认子代理分别选择模型的设置界面。delegate_skill 可把任务连同技能正文交给子代理；预设还包含构思、计划、测试驱动开发、调试与评审等工作流技能。适合希望将开发流程方法与子代理模型分开配置的 DSH 用户。安装插件即可加入预设；源码未要求额外 API key。

DSH Superpowers is a web preset for spec-driven development. It bundles Superpowers skills, a persona, skill delegation, and per-skill model routing. It suits DSH users who want structured workflows and different models for child agents. No extra API key is required.
想让不同开发技能的子代理使用不同模型。
在 DSH 里按规格先设计计划，再分派编码任务给子代理。
I need a DSH workflow preset with test-driven development, debugging, and code review skills.
DSH Superpowers 的功能「按技能路由子代理模型」：设置页可为技能及未绑定技能的其他子代理配置 provider 和 model；delegate_skill 根据技能配置启动子代理，未配置时继承父会话模型。
DSH Superpowers 的功能「委派 Superpowers 技能」：delegate_skill 接收技能、任务和任务说明，读取对应技能正文并启动子代理，等待完成后返回文本结果及使用的模型信息。

@goodjin2/dsh-superpowers README · dsh-superpowers：The problem it solves: Superpowers is a heavily skill-based methodology, but in a
default harness every subagent runs on whatever model the parent is using. Running
`systematic-debugging` on a big model and `writing-good-tests` on a cheap one is the
obvious thing to want, and there is no first-class way to get it.

@goodjin2/dsh-superpowers README · What you get：| | |
|---|---|
| **A preset, not just a plugin** | Ships the 15 Superpowers skills and the persona that makes the agent actually follow the six-phase method |
| **Per-skill model settings** | A Superpowers section in Settings: one dropdown per skill, plus a row for subagents that aren't bound to a skill |
| **One dispatch tool** | `delegate_skill` — reads the table, starts the child on that model, names the child session after the skill |
| **The model is visible** | A subagent's composer shows which model it is actually running on, read-only |
| **It cannot break your install** | The host row is fault-tolerant by construction; DSH starts and stays usable even if this plugin fails entirely |

@goodjin2/dsh-superpowers README · Install：Two halves, two steps. The **plugin** is global — Settings section, model
table, tool module, self-check. The **preset** is the selectable mode —
skills, persona, tool rows. On DSH 0.2.x the preset ships WITH the package as a
declaration row, so installing is all it takes.

From GitHub (the package is not on npm — install straight from the repository):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add goodjin/dsh-superpowers
```

@goodjin2/dsh-superpowers README · Install：That is the whole install: **Superpowers** appears in the preset selector.
(Older DSH builds read the preset from `~/.dsh/.agent-presets/superpowers/`;
0.2.x does not, so there is no directory to copy.)

To make it the default preset:

```yaml
agent-presets:
  default: superpowers
```

Otherwise just pick **Superpowers** from the preset selector in the UI.

@goodjin2/dsh-superpowers README · Configure：Open **Settings → Superpowers**. Each row is one skill; the last row covers
subagents dispatched without a skill. Choices are read on the next dispatch — no
restart, no preset edit.

Routes are stored in the profile patch's `superpowers-delegation-settings`
loader row (DSH 0.2.x keeps plugin config there, not in `settings.yaml`), so you
can also edit them by hand in `cordis.patch.yml`:

@goodjin2/dsh-superpowers README · Configure：```yaml
- id: superpowers-delegation-settings
  name: "@goodjin2/dsh-superpowers"
  config:
    defaultProvider: minimax-cn

Values set in `settings.yaml` before upgrading are migrated automatically on
first boot — the migration only fills fields you have not already set, so it
never overwrites a later hand-edit.

@goodjin2/dsh-superpowers README · Configure：Resolution order per skill: the skill's own pin (including「复用主会话模型」,
which is stored as a sentinel and omits `agentOptions` so the child uses the
parent session's model), then the default pair from the「其他子代理」row (same
sentinel supported), then nothing — which also inherits the parent's route.
Settings「跟随默认」on a skill row clears that skill's pin so the default pair
applies; it is not the same as「复用主会话模型」, which is honored even when a
default pair is configured.

@goodjin2/dsh-superpowers README · Verifying an install：```sh
node ~/.dsh/profiles/web/node_modules/@goodjin2/dsh-superpowers/scripts/check.mjs 3080 <token>
```

The token is in the URL you opened DSH with; it changes on every restart. The
check reports each host-side dependency this plugin has, individually. After a
DSH upgrade, run it first — see below.

@goodjin2/dsh-superpowers README · Verifying an install：The key line is `route.exists`: it POSTs the browser channel directly. When the
host half silently failed to register its route (the bug fixed in v0.2.1), the
row stayed "active", nothing logged anything, and only this probe could see the
404. Do not skip it.

@goodjin2/dsh-superpowers README · Upgrades and compatibility：DSH has no per-plugin version pinning: the plugin is resolved from the profile at
start. A DSH upgrade that moves an internal API produces **no error** — the server
boots and this feature quietly stops working. That is the failure mode this plugin
was built to survive rather than to prevent.

@goodjin2/dsh-superpowers README · Upgrades and compatibility：**Supported DSH versions:** `>=0.1.5-rc.2 <0.3.0` (declared in `peerDependencies`
as `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools`). Outside that range the Desktop plugin panel marks
the plugin incompatible and blocks activation — that gate is the only signal this
plugin gets when DSH moves under it.

@goodjin2/dsh-superpowers README · Upgrades and compatibility：- **The host row is wrapped so it cannot stop DSH from starting.** Verified by
  fault injection: with the row throwing, DSH boots and all 54 client entries
  still mount. The plugin degrades to "no per-skill pins".
- **The settings page shows a self-check line at the top of the Superpowers
  section** — green when every dependency is where the plugin expects it, red with
  a per-item explanation when not.
- **Client-side failures are isolated per entry** by the host's plugin loader, so a
  broken client half shows a banner and leaves the rest of the UI working.
@goodjin2/dsh-superpowers README · Upgrades and compatibility：If the check reports a failure, the item name tells you which dependency moved.

@goodjin2/dsh-superpowers README · Layout：| Path | |
|---|---|
| `lib/index.js` | Host row: settings namespace, the browser channel, the self-check endpoint |
| `lib/client.js` | Browser row: the Settings section, the composer model label |
| `lib/skill-delegation.js` | The `delegate_skill` tool |
| `lib/settings-schema.js` | The stored settings shape and route resolution |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | The two composition rows this plugin adds |
| `preset/` | The agent preset and the 15 Superpowers skills |
| `scripts/check.mjs` | Post-upgrade compatibility check |
| `scripts/test.mjs` | Load-safety and degradation tests, run in the checkout and against the installed copy |

@goodjin2/dsh-superpowers README · Version anchor tags：This repo participates in the container's DSH version-correspondence mechanism: every
plugin repo carries tags named `dsh-<dsh版本>` (e.g. `dsh-0.2.2-rc.1`), each an annotated
tag recording the dsh version it was verified against, the check result, and the date.
The tag is the immutable "known-good coordinate" of that dsh version — a snapshot of
`main` taken the moment the whole-plugin row check went green on every installed host.

@goodjin2/dsh-superpowers README · Version anchor tags：- **Why tags instead of releases**: the desktop app reads this checkout by path and the
  web install pulls `repo#ref` — a git tag is already the furthest installable form, so
  no npm publish or GitHub Release is needed.
- **Rollback**: `scripts/pin-to-dsh.sh 0.2.2-rc.1` (from the container) checks out the
  tag in every repo at once; `scripts/check-host-rows.mjs --report` shows which repos are
  on the anchor for the running dsh version.
- **Do not move or delete a `dsh-*` tag**; it is a rollback coordinate. A follow-up fix on
  the same dsh version adds a `-p2` (then `-p3`) suffixed tag instead.
- New tags are cut after each dsh upgrade, as step 4 of the upgrade runbook — see the
  container's `AGENTS.md` for the full flow.
